Article Title: 'Safe and speedy return of Rohingya': India reiterates stand after Myanmar ICJ verdict
Article Text:
India has reiterated its commitment to aiding the safe and sustainable repatriation of Rohingya Muslims to Myanmar, following the International Court of Justice's recent ruling on genocide against this community in 2017

NEW DELHI: India on Friday reiterated its support for the safe and sustainable return of the displaced Rohingya muslims to Myanmar. The statement came a day after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) delivered its landmark verdict in the genocide case against Myanmar.Addressing a media briefing, ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said India had consistently supported the "safe, speedy and sustainable return" of displaced Rohingys.He also highlighted India's humanitarian assistance to Rohingya refugees living in camps in Bangladesh, saying New Delhi had provided relief supplies in five consignments under Operation Insaniyat. Jaiswal also referred to India's development assistance programmes in Myanmar.India's humanitarian assistance to the Rohingya crisis dates back to September 2017, when it launched Operation Insaniyat to support Bangladesh in managing the influx of refugees fleeing Myanmar.According to the MEA's 2017-18 annual report, India supplied essential relief materials to around 3 lakh displaced people, including rice, pulses, sugar, salt, cooking oil, tea, ready-to-eat food, biscuits and mosquito nets.India also provided relief supplies to around 15,000 displaced people in Myanmar during October and November 2017, according to a written reply by the government in Parliament.Separately, India committed $25 million over five years under the Rakhine State Development Programme to support socio-economic development in Myanmar's Rakhine State.As part of the initiative, India handed over 250 prefabricated houses in July 2019 for displaced people returning from Bangladesh. Its assistance also included agricultural equipment, 40 computers for Sittwe Computer University and medical equipment for Sittwe General Hospital. In December 2019, India provided 20,000 relief kits to internally displaced people in Rakhine State.The International Court of Justice (ICJ), the United Nations' highest court, on Thursday ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority during the military's 2017 clearance operations in northern Rakhine State.The judgment, delivered by a 9-6 majority in a case brought by The Gambia in 2019, marks the first time the court has held a state responsible for committing genocide.The court found that Myanmar violated its obligations under the 1948 Genocide Convention by failing to prevent and punish genocide and by not taking adequate steps to preserve evidence of the atrocities.It ordered Myanmar to investigate and prosecute those suspected of involvement, prevent further violations, provide guarantees against repetition and compensate the Rohingya victims.The ruling also called for restitution, including the safe, voluntary and dignified return of displaced Rohingya and reunification of families. The amount and modalities of compensation will be decided in a subsequent phase, with Myanmar required to submit a report to the court within two years.
Article Summary: India reiterates its support for the safe and sustainable return of the displaced Rohingya muslims to Myanmar. The statement came a day after the International Court of Justice (ICJ) delivered its landmark verdict in the genocide case against Myanmar. India's humanitarian assistance to the Rohingya crisis dates back to September 2017.

Article Title: ‘Don’t make statements against country’: Rijiju’s message to Rahul Gandhi
Article Text:
Rijiju hits out at Rahul over ‘side player’ remark

NEW DELHI: Union minister Kiren Rijiju on Friday urged Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi not to make statements against the country, either in India or abroad, following his remarks describing India as a "side player" in global affairs and questioning its role in diplomatic efforts between the United States and Iran."I would just request him not to make statements against the country, whether inside India or abroad. That is all I want to say," Rijiju said.The BJP also accused Rahul of being "obsessed with Pakistan ", alleging that he had portrayed the neighbouring country as a role model in his assessment of India's foreign policy.In a series of posts on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari criticised Gandhi's remarks during an interaction with students at the University of Chicago on Wednesday."Why is Rahul Gandhi so obsessed with Pakistan! At every global stage Rahul acts like Pak Fan Boy!" Bhandari said."Yet again he idolizes Pakistan as a role model for him in foreign policy outreach!" he added.Bhandari alleged that Rahul's "love for Pakistan" had led him to overlook India's diplomatic efforts, including its peace initiatives in the Russia-Ukraine conflict."His love for Pakistan has made him forget that it is India which Russia and Ukraine both acknowledged for its peace efforts and Iran waived of any Hormuz restrictions," he said."Rahul Gandhi's love for terror state Pakistan made UPA compromise India's sovereignty at Sharmal Shekh and not attack Pakistan post 26/11 terror attack!" Bhandari added.During his interaction at the University of Chicago, Rahul said India had traditionally maintained a sophisticated understanding of geopolitics but had increasingly become a "side player" in global affairs.He questioned why Pakistan was involved in facilitating negotiations between the US and Iran while India, given its size and international standing, appeared to be on the sidelines."India, by its size, naturally has a global voice and India should be actively involved in global conversations. But frankly, India has become a side player," Gandhi said.He also referred to India's historical role in international affairs, particularly through the Non-Aligned Movement, and argued that the country should seek to regain a more active position in global diplomacy.Criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's foreign policy approach, Rahul said personal relationships between world leaders could not determine a country's geopolitical standing."Friendship is not the point. Who gives a damn about friendship? Do you really think that geopolitics is going to work because the guy is your friend? He's leading a structure. He's got a whole economic system under him. He's not going to make decisions based on whether he likes you or doesn't like you. So these are some of the things that disturb me," he said.Clarifying his position on personal relationships between political leaders, Rahul added, "I don't have a problem with being friends with Mr Modi or being friends with leaders. Friendship is not that important. What's important is that you understand what's going on, who you are, and where you fit."
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju urges Rahul Gandhi not to make statements against the country. Gandhi described India as a "side player" in global affairs. He questioned India's role in diplomatic efforts between the U.S. and Iran. The BJP accused Rahul of being "obsessed with Pakistan"

Article Title: PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, offers condolences over mother's death
Article Text:
PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, condoles death of his mother

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday spoke to Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath and expressed condolences over the death of his mother, Savitri Devi , who passed away at the age of 91 in her native village in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district.Savitri Devi died around 10.45 am on Friday in Panchur village, residents told PTI. She had been unwell for a long time and could recognise only family members, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha said.Pauri Garhwal Senior Superintendent of Police Sarvesh Panwar said the local administration was in touch with the family.Adityanath was attending a public function in Uttar Pradesh when he received the news of his mother's death. He had two more official engagements scheduled for later in the day and was expected to continue with his programme. It was not immediately clear whether he would travel to Uttarakhand for the last rites, which are likely to be held on Saturday.G C Badola, a member of the Panchur Gram Sabha, told PTI, “One of her sons is posted in Kotdwar and will reach the village by Friday evening. The last rites will likely be conducted at Phool Chatti Ghat near the village on Saturday, where the last rites of Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s father were also held.”Defence minister Rajnath Singh expressed grief over Savitri Devi's death in a post on X, saying the loss of a mother was one of the most unbearable blows in life. He extended his condolences to Adityanath and his family.Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami also described her death as extremely sad and heartbreaking, saying, "Her demise is an irreparable loss to the family." He extended his condolences to the bereaved family and prayed for strength for them to cope with the loss.Uttar Pradesh Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak, along with state BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary, also condoled her death and prayed for peace for the departed soul and strength for the family.Adityanath's father, Anand Singh Bisht, died following a prolonged illness in 2020. His last rites were performed in Uttarakhand. Adityanath did not attend the funeral due to the Covid-19 lockdown and his responsibilities as Uttar Pradesh chief minister.
Article Summary: PM Modi speaks to Yogi Adityanath, condoles death of his mother Savitri Devi. She died at the age of 91 in her native village in Uttarakhand's Pauri Garhwal district. Last rites will likely be conducted at Phool Chatti Ghat near the village on Saturday.

Article Title: 'Rubbing salt into Pahalgam victims' wounds': Row over Pakistan minister at SCO meet in Delhi

NEW DELHI: A political row broke out after Pakistan minister Masood Malik arrived in Delhi on Friday to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. Congress questioned the invitation and accused the BJP-led Centre of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victims’ families”."You keep changing your stance. Sometimes you travel there, sometimes you reach Lahore, at other times you abruptly call off Operation Sindoor, and now you invite them here. What exactly is Prime Minister Modi doing? The funeral pyres of those martyred in the Pahalgam massacre have not even cooled yet, and you are rubbing salt into the wounds of their families,” said Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate."The Government of India, led by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, is organising the SCO Civilisational Dialogue in India on November 21 and 22. The question is: why was Pakistan invited to this event? Why have you invited Pakistan, a country that sponsors terrorism in India? You invited Pakistan, and its minister, Musadik Malik, has arrived here," she said.Questioning the "red carpet" treatment being extended to the minister, Shrinate said, "This is the same person who had openly threatened just a few months ago to chop off the hands of Indians and shed our blood.""The question is that Pakistan has not stopped sponsoring terrorism, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government is busy welcoming its representatives. Musadik Malik be served biryani, kebabs and kheer? The government is rolling out the red carpet to welcome him. Why does your work not get done without an anti-India Pakistan? The point is that you should also say and do what Rahul Gandhi has stated unequivocally: as long as Pakistan continues to sponsor terrorism, no dialogue with it is possible," she added.J&K Congress President Tariq Hameed Karra also accused the BJP of having "double standards" regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties."Look, as far as the Government of India is concerned, particularly the BJP,ey have always had double standards. Whether it is regarding militancy, Indo-Pakistan talks, or international treaties, their approach has consistently been marked by double standards. The very person who made the loudest protests when the Indus Waters Treaty was suspended here had raised more objections than anyone else at that time. But the fact that they are displaying double standards is nothing new," he said."This is another example of their double standards. When our Prime Minister went to Pakistan uninvited, what could be a bigger example of double standards than that? Basically, the BJP has lost its track.Its foreign policy is being handled on a day-to-day basis. It has no consistent or permanent policy towards its neighbouring countries, whether Pakistan, China, Bangladesh or Sri Lanka. They deal with each country according to what suits them at a particular time," he added.Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi to attend the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisation Dialogue. He was received by Pakistan high commissioner's Chargé d'Affaires in India, Saad Warraich. Malik's visit marks the first time a Pakistani minister has travelled to India in three years.
Article Summary: Congress leaders criticised the Centre over Pakistan minister Masood Malik's visit to Delhi for the SCO Civilisation Dialogue. Congress accused the BJP-led Centre of “rubbing salt into the wounds of Pahalgam victims’ families”

When my team researched your work, we discovered perhaps the world's most unusual restaurant - your langar.(Laughs) Well, Sanjiv, we certainly haven't had a “reservations desk” in our langar for the last 3 decades! The reason is simple: hunger doesn't make appointmentsAnyone can come to my home and receive food. No application. No appointment. No eligibility test! To me, it is one of the most natural and satisfying things to do.You have experienced wealth and yet you say that your langar gives you a satisfaction no amount of wealth can buy. Isn't this a paradox?Only if we assume that everything valuable has a price! (Laughs). A meal has a price. A blessing doesn't come with a price tag! Sanjiv, I don't really think of myself as giving anything. I am simply sharing my abundance. Service comes naturally to me. It is my joy. That is why I often say to myself: Feed. Feed. Feed.You make feeding sound almost spiritual. Is that why Annapurna resonates so strongly with your philosophy?Annapurna represents something beautiful in our tradition - the assurance that nobody should remain hungry. To me, that also means responsibility. If the Universe has been generous to us, surely, we can share that abundance with others?Take a hospital, for example. While doctors care for patients, who looks after their families? That is what led me to become involved in pioneering community kitchens serving patients' families outside AIIMS (All India Institute of Medical Sciences), New Delhi.And how did water become part of your mission?: (Laughs) Sanjiv, when someone is thirsty in 45-degree heat, they don't need a lecture on climate change. They need a glass of cool water!When the Delhi Heat Action Plan was launched by the Chief Minister. Rekha Gupta, I was delighted to be invited by Rajendra Singh of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, to support the initiative through digital cool-water dispensing machines. Impact doesn't have to be glamorous. It has to be useful!Could your philosophy ofhelp bridge the rural -urban divide?Absolutely! The people constructing and maintaining our homes and cities often come from distant villages.As fellow Bharatwasis, isn't it our responsibility to ensure that they receive fresh, nutritious food, are paid generously for their services and are treated with dignity?And I mean proper nutrition - wholesome, preferably home-cooked food prepared with good ingredients and healthy oils.Think of a migrant worker who has come to a city to earn a livelihood but has no kitchen of his own. If we provide him with fresh, nutritious food, he not only stays healthier but can also save more of his hard-earned income. And where do those savings go? Back to his family in the village! That money flows into rural Bharat, supporting families, strengthening local businesses and, as it circulates through village economies, potentially contributing to better housing, facilities and infrastructure.Our cities have infrastructure that many of our villages still lack. What if we could help bridge that gap through something as simple as sharing nutritious food? Every migrant worker is a human bridge between rural and urban Bharat. If we strengthen that bridge, we strengthen Bharat itself!And Sanjiv, life is a mirror. When we help others grow, we grow too.That is why I believecan become something much larger than a meal.That sounds like a much bigger idea than feeding people. Are you suggesting that Anna is also about how we treat one another?Precisely! Anna begins with food, but it cannot end there. What good is a meal if we deny someone dignity? We must recognise that the people who serve us are our fellow Bharatiyas. Their nutrition, welfare and dignity should matter to us. Pay them generously. Feed them nutritiously. Treat them respectfully, with dignityI find the thinking of Nobel Laureate and Harvard University Professor Amartya Sen particularly profound: development is not merely about rising incomes, but about expanding people's real freedoms - including the freedom to live without hunger. After all, what meaning does prosperity have if people are still denied the basic dignity of a nutritious meal?But isn't hunger fundamentally the government's responsibility?A government can create a food-security system. Citizens help create a culture in which nobody's hunger is ignored. I believe that caring for our fellow citizens is a personal responsibility, not merely an act of generosity. It is a moral commitment. That is the Bharat I would love to see. I believe we need to rediscover a very personal relationship with our country. Every morning, why not ask ourselves one little question: What can I do today to make my Bharat a little better?But how do we turn that sentiment into something practical?(Laughs) Ah, Sanjiv! We Bharatiyas are very good at slogans. Sometimes we need to be equally good at acting upon them!Let us start with a small deed, not a big program:Each one, feed one!Finally, how does Anna fit into your larger vision of Viksit Bharat 2047?Sanjiv, along with economic growth, technology and global influence, we must nourish our workers and our future generations. A well-nourished Bharat is the foundation of a Viksit Bharat.I have always loved the writings of Ralph Waldo Emerson. One thought I draw from his philosophy is that when we hold a powerful vision and act upon it with conviction, the world around us can begin to move in that direction. I believe that when we send a thought of goodness into the Universe, and follow it with action, we help make that goodness a reality. I dream of a healthy nation.Four hundred cities. Sixteen thousand villages. Millions of lives touched by one simple idea: Each One, Feed One! That is my dream for Bharat. And Sanjiv, I can see it happening!You may possess the Kohinoor, but what good will it do you when it cannot give you a blessing? Feed a hungry person, and you will definitely receive a blessing that no diamond can ever give.(Laughs) So my message is simple: Live consciously. Look beyond yourself. Each one, feed one.
Article Summary: Sanjiv Kaura, CEO-CSR, The Times of India, talks to Aruna Lohia Goenka about her YASHA framework for India. The framework includes Shiksha (education), Yuva (youth), Hunar (skills) and Abundance (shared prosperity) Share your thoughts in the comments.

NEW DELHI: A claim by Pakistani think tank analyst that no Indian official was present to receive Pakistan's minister Musadik Masood Malik, upon his arrival in New Delhi has been contradicted by official sources cited by news agency ANI.Khurram Abbas alleged that India had not extended the customary official welcome to Malik, who arrived in the national capital on Thursday to attend the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum."India didn’t show courtesy to send official to welcome Pakistan climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Malik who arrived in Delhi to attend SCO meeting. He was welcomed by the Pakistani CdA. First Pakistan minister in India since 2023 & May 2025 conflict," Abbas alleged in a post on X.However, according to sources cited by news agency ANI, a director from the Union ministry of culture and an under secretary from the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the MEA were present at the airport to receive Malik as part of the welcome protocol.The sources also clarified that all SCO member countries arriving in New Delhi were being extended a similar level of protocol.Malik's visit is significant as he is the first Pakistani minister to travel to India in three years and the first since the May 2025 military confrontation between the two nuclear-armed countries following the Pahalgam terror attack , in which 26 people were killed by Pakistan-backed terrorists in Jammu and Kashmir The last high-profile visit by a Pakistani political leader was that of then-foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari in 2023.Malik is in New Delhi to participate in the thematic sessions of the first SCO Civilisational Dialogue Forum, scheduled to be held from November 20 to 22.According to Pakistan's ministry of foreign affairs, Malik will represent Islamabad at the forum and present Pakistan's perspective on the importance of dialogue among civilisations and its role in diplomacy.In a statement, the ministry said the minister's address would highlight Pakistan's constructive role in the SCO, along with the country's diverse civilisational and cultural heritage."Pakistan's participation in this Forum is reflective of its contribution as an active State to promote dialogue, cooperation and understanding in line with the 'Shanghai Spirit'," the statement said.Pakistan's participation follows India's invitation to all 10 SCO member states, along with observer countries and dialogue partners, to attend the inaugural forum.The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had earlier confirmed that several countries, including SCO member states, had been invited to the event, adding that New Delhi looked forward to hosting the dialogue.Proposed by India, the initiative aims to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties across the Eurasian region.Defence minister Rajnath Singh had announced India's plan to host the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum while addressing the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20.The SCO has 10 member states, including India, Pakistan, China and Russia. India became a full member of the grouping in 2017.
Article Summary: Pakistan's climate change and environmental coordination minister Musadik Masood Malik arrived in New Delhi on Thursday. Malik is in India to attend the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum. Think tank analyst Khurram Abbas alleged that India had not extended the customary official welcome to Malik. But sources cited by news agency ANI said an under secretary from the Pakistan, Afghanistan and Iran (PAI) division of the MEA was present at the airport.

NEW DELHI: In a setback to the Karnataka government, the Supreme Court on Friday refused to interfere with a state high court ruling that permits bike taxi services to operate across Karnataka.A bench of Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N Kotiswar Singh dismissed the state's appeal, thereby retaining the relief granted to bike taxi aggregators and operators by the Karnataka High Court, news agency ANI reported.The case dates back to an earlier order that had asked bike taxi operators to halt services until the state introduced a regulatory framework. However, on January 23, 2026, a division bench of the high court, then headed by Chief Justice Vibhu Bakhru and comprising Justice CM Joshi, overturned that direction.The high court's ruling came on appeals by Ola , Uber, Rapido, motorcycle owners and the Bike Taxi Welfare Association. It said motorcycles could be registered as transport vehicles and used as contract carriages, provided they complied with the state's regulatory requirements.The state government subsequently approached the apex court, arguing that the operation of bike taxis raised concerns about passenger safety, insurance protection and the absence of adequate safeguards.Traditional auto and taxi driver associations had also opposed the move, contending that bike taxi operators should not be allowed to function without meeting regulatory obligations comparable to those imposed on conventional transport services.
Article Summary: Supreme Court refuses to interfere with state high court ruling that permits bike taxi services to operate across Karnataka. Article Title: Old Monk maker Mohan Meakin, India’s largest rum maker, faces revenue setback after FSSAI questions the composition and labelling of three rum variants produced at its Maharashtra facility; revenue dr
Article Text:
FSSAI also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’. (Image source: Mohan Meakin wesbite)

FSSAI sales restrictions on some Old Monk variants

India’s largest rum maker by volume, Mohan Meakin, which is known for its Old Monk has taken a serious revenue hit. The company saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year after food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility.The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.The unlisted company’s revenue from operations dropped 64% to Rs 288 crore during April-September, compared with Rs 792 crore in the corresponding period a year earlier, according to its latest financial results. The contraction was even steeper in the September quarter, with revenue falling 77% year-on-year to Rs 108 crore from Rs 473 crore.The sales restrictions were imposed after the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) inspected the company’s manufacturing facility in Khopoli, according to an ET report..The regulator objected to the use of neutral spirit blended with rum flavouring, contending that such products could not be marketed as conventional rum and should instead be classified as rum-flavoured spirits.It also raised objections to product descriptions such as ‘7 Years Old Blended’ and ‘Very Old Vatted’.The facility has remained shut since May, according to the financial daily.Mohan Rocky Springwater Breweries, the company that is responsible for manufacturing and bottling Old Monk in Maharashtra, challenged the FSSAI order before the Bombay High Court.However, it withdrew its petition on November 5, informing the court that it would submit revised labels directly to the regulator for approval. The court disposed of the petition as not pressed, leaving the sales restrictions in place.Mohan Meakin had earlier agreed to drop the claim that the rum had been aged for seven years and make information about the addition of flavouring more prominent on its labels. The regulator, however, maintained that the central dispute concerned how the product itself should be classified.At an October hearing, the company’s lawyers told the court that the restrictions had resulted in losses of around Rs 50 crore for the company and deprived the Maharashtra government of nearly Rs 350 crore in excise revenue. They also said that about 300 workers had been left without work.The regulatory setback comes at a time when Mohan Meakin has been working to restore Old Monk’s market position following years of declining sales, as whisky has gained dominance in India’s liquor market.The brand, which is around seven decades old and has long been associated with winter drinking, hostel rooftops and military canteens, saw its annual sales volume decline to 4.1 million cases in 2013 from a peak of 8 million cases in 2002.Sales subsequently recovered, and two years ago, Old Monk overtook United Spirits’ McDowell’s No. 1 Celebration to become India’s largest-selling rum brand by volume. The brand sold 14 million cases in 2025.The turnaround followed a leadership change after Brigadier Kapil Mohan, the company’s long-serving chairman, died in 2018.
Article Summary: Mohan Meakin saw its revenue more than halve in the first six months of the current financial year. Food safety authorities stopped sales of three Old Monk variants which are produced at its Maharashtra facility. The regulator raised concerns about the products’ composition and whether they qualified to be sold as rum.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, remembering her contributions to the country.Taking to X, PM shared a brief message marking the occasion. "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary," he posted.Several Congress leaders, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party president Mallikarjun Kharge, also remembered the country's first and only woman prime minister.Rahul Gandhi paid tribute to his grandmother by sharing a conversation between his mother, Sonia Gandhi, and sister, Priyanka, about Indira Gandhi.He wrote on X: "Dadi was formidable: fearless, resilient, and full of love. Her strength lives on in the women of my family, each one unique and brilliant in her own way. Their love and warmth hold us together, and they inspire me every single day.""Happy birthday, Dadi. You would be so proud of them," he added.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra also paid tribute to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary, describing her as a "tigress" and saying there would never be another leader like her.“Happy Birthday, tigress! There will never be another like you,” Priyanka Gandhi posted on X.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi and other senior leaders also paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her birth anniversary at the central hall of Samvidhan Sadan in New Delhi. Karnataka chief minister D K Shivakumar also marked the occasion with a tribute, describing Indira Gandhi as the “Iron Lady”. He highlighted her role in shaping India's political and economic landscape during her years in office.In his message on X, the Karnataka chief minister pointed to her contributions to agriculture, banking and the country's space and nuclear programmes. He said her tenure saw several major developments that influenced India's growth.Shivakumar added that PM Indira Gandhi continued to hold an important place in the country's post-independence history. He said her contribution to India's political journey and development would be remembered with respect.The tributes came as the country marked the birth anniversary of one of India's most prominent political leaders, Indira Gandhi, who was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, now Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh and the daughter of India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru. She served until her assassination in 1984. Her son, Rajiv Gandhi, took over as Prime Minister after her death.

Article Title: One boundary at a time, Yashasvi Jaiswal deflates New Zealand
Article Text:
Yashasvi Jaiswal (Pic credit: BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief Scores

New Zealand 1st innings: 368 all out in 121 overs (Henry Nicholls 175, Glenn Phillips 118; Jasprit Bumrah 4/92, Akash Deep 3/53)

India 1st innings: 159 for 1 after 39 overs (Yashasvi Jaiswal 85, KL Rahul 52 batting; Matt Henry 1/43)

WELLINGTON: Straight as an arrow, Yashasvi Jaiswal smoked one past Jacob Duffy to bring up his half-century off 66 balls. Another boundary, a rare scratchy one, followed the next ball as the southpaw moved to 54 with his tenth four of the innings. India had already surpassed their previous best opening stand of 73 in this part of the world, dating back to 2009, and Jaiswal was throwing punches with sublime strokeplay.There were no half-measures. He drove beautifully, wasn't afraid to deploy the ramp and kept finding gaps with ease against New Zealand's seamers. The left-handed batter operated with a lot of assurance after giving the new ball the required respect and never looked back. There was a lot of arrogance in the way he went about his business, bordering on audacity against a potent bowling attack featuring Jacob Duffy, Kyle Jamieson and Nathan Smith.The calmness of KL Rahul at the other end was the perfect antidote as the two stitched together a fluent partnership to give India a solid start to their innings. Rahul was lucky to survive an LBW shout early in the innings, but he hardly drew attention as Jaiswal stepped on the gas. The 24-year-old hit 16 boundaries during his knock, and his intent after reaching his half-century blew the Kiwis away.The next 35 runs came off just 32 deliveries, with 28 of those runs scored in boundaries.Jacob Duffy struggled, and Jaiswal never allowed any fast bowler in the opposition camp to find rhythm. His footwork remained precise, and his shot selection was impeccable. Except for that wild hoick moments after his fifty, Jaiswal largely played on merit and operated with a watertight defence off the back foot.The youngster featured in three India A-New Zealand A fixtures before the Test series and came well prepared for the two-match series. His starts in those fixtures were subdued, but he roared back with scores of 155* and 102 and carried the confidence from those games into the Wellington opener. Jaiswal's runs and intent not only wiped off the valuable deficit but also deflated the opposition by not allowing them an opportunity to stitch together a plan.With nothing happening off the surface or in the air, and the ball losing its sheen off Jaiswal's willow, the hosts threw a desperate dice by bringing the wicketkeeper up to the opener. Not that Jaiswal was walking into his shots, but it was just an attempt to make things happen when he wasn't allowing anything to happen.The move gave the hosts their first and only success of the day as Jaiswal nicked one to Tom Blundell off Matt Henry to end his entertaining 89-ball essay. Head down, he dragged himself back to the dressing room to a roaring applause, well aware that a big score was there for the taking. His 85 helped India put 130 on the board in just 27.5 overs and could well have delivered a decisive blow to the opposition.
Article Summary: Yashasvi Jaiswal scores 85 as India reach 159-1 in their first innings. The wicketkeeper hit 16 boundaries in an entertaining 89-ball essay. New Zealand were bowled out for 368, with Henry Nicholls scoring 175.

Article Title: No transactions made, no OTPs shared: Bengaluru techie loses Rs 5.5L in AMEX, RBL card fraud
Article Text:
AI Image Used For Representational Purpose Only

Similar Crime:

One minute, three transactions: Man loses Rs 3.4L

How to stay safe

Disable international transactions: Keep international usage switched off unless required. Enable it only when making overseas payments.

Set transaction limits: Set lower spending limits for online, contactless and international transactions. Increase them temporarily when necessary.

Never share card details: Do not disclose your card number, CVV, expiry date, PIN or OTP to anyone, including people claiming to represent banks.

Avoid suspicious links: Do not click on links received through SMS, WhatsApp, emails or social media that promise rewards, refunds, credit card upgrades or fee waivers.

Do not install unknown APK files: Avoid downloading applications from unverified websites or links. Never grant unnecessary permissions to applications.

Avoid public Wi-Fi for payments: Do not access banking applications or make financial transactions through unsecured public Wi-Fi networks.





BENGALURU: A 31-year-old software engineer lost Rs 5.5 lakh in a credit card fraud involving his AMEX and RBL Bank cards on Nov 11, after cybercriminals allegedly carried out multiple unauthorised transactions within just an hour.According to the complaint filed by Siddarth (name changed), a resident of Indiranagar, fraudulent transactions worth Rs 4,02,722 were made on his AMEX credit card, while Rs 1,44,558 was debited from his RBL Bank card. The transactions took place between 12.56 pm and 2 pm, taking the total loss to Rs 5,47,280.Siddarth told police that neither he nor his family members had shared their card details, OTPs, PINs or other confidential banking information with anyone. He also denied downloading any APK files or authorising transactions.The family became aware of the fraud after receiving notifications about the suspicious transactions. Siddarth immediately contacted both banks, got the cards blocked to prevent further losses and reported the incident to the national cybercrime helpline 1930 before approaching police.A case has been registered at the East Cyber Crime police station under the Information Technology Act and Section 318 (cheating) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).Why do such frauds happen?Credit card frauds involving unauthorised transactions can occur even when victims insist they have not shared their OTPs, PINs or card details. In many cases, fraudsters exploit weaknesses in digital payment systems, steal card information through sophisticated methods or misuse compromised credentials, the officer said.However, in this case, investigation will have to establish how the card details were accessed and how the payments were authorised, he added.Another senior officer said the possibilities of siphoning off money from credit cards include card data theft: Fraudsters may obtain card numbers, expiry dates and CVV details through compromised websites, data breaches, phishing links or fake payment gateways. Compromised online platforms: If an online shopping website, payment gateway or merchant account is compromised, stored card information may be exposed.Three back-to-back transactions within a minute cost a 30-year-old private firm employee Rs 3.4 lakh after fraudsters misused his credit card, which he claimed he had not used for the last five months. He received alerts for all three transactions together while he was on a phone call on Nov 6. He immediately contacted the card support team and reported the fraud.Rehman (name changed) from Lingarajapura said the transactions included Rs 1,36,996 at Innovative Retail Concept (BigBasket), Rs 39,200 at Php Indus Appstore Private and Rs 1,64,852 at Blinkit.He said he had neither made nor approved the payments; he had not received or shared any OTP.
Article Summary: A 31-year-old software engineer lost Rs 5.5 lakh in a credit card fraud involving his AMEX and RBL Bank cards on Nov 11. The transactions took place between 12.56 pm and 2 pm, taking the total loss to Rs 5,47,280. Fraudsters allegedly carried out multiple unauthorised transactions within just an hour.

NEW DELHI: A 12-year-old boy was killed after being run over by a bulldozer that was returning from a Samajwadi Party (SP) roadshow led by party supremo Akhilesh Yadav in Uttar Pradesh 's Gorakhpur . The SP, however, refuted all charges and claimed that the incident took place after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved past the area. The SP media cell also shared CCTV footage of the incident to back-up their claim.Former UP CM Akhilesh Yadav had received a grand 'bulldozer welcome' during his PDA 'rath yatra' in Yogi Adityanath's bastion, Gorakhpur on Wednesday.The deceased, identified as Aryavardhan Singh, was a resident of Rajdhani village in Chauri Chaura. His father is a local BJP leader. The incident took place in the Koodaghat area during the SP's Rath Yatra, officials told IANS.According to the boy's father, Omkar Singh, the bulldozer was showering flower petals on the rally when it hit his son. He alleged that Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had already moved ahead when the bulldozer, which was approaching at high speed, struck the boy from behind.Speaking to news agency IANS, Omkar Singh said, "Around 2pm, when Akhilesh Yadav's convoy passed, my son was going to pick up his sister from Kendriya Vidyalaya.While he was crossing the road, Akhilesh Yadav's convoy had moved ahead.""A flower-showering JCB was following the convoy at a very high speed so that flowers could be showered on Akhilesh Yadav from behind. During that time, my son was crossing the road when the JCB ran over him. He died on the spot," he added.The impact of the collision reportedly flung Aryavardhan towards a road divider, leaving him with a severe injury to the back of his head. He later succumbed to his injuries.The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow and criticised the behaviour of SP supporters during the procession.In a statement, the UP BJP said, "In Gorakhpur, SP supporters, in their frenzy to welcome Akhilesh Yadav, took the life of an innocent 12-year-old child! The child died a painful death after being hit by a JCB during the PDA chariot procession -- the result of SP supporters' rowdiness and irresponsible behaviour.""This is what they're like while out of power; imagine the havoc they'll wreak once they come to power! Should we call them SP supporters or hooligans? Is a show of power more precious to them than an innocent child's life?" it added.An investigation into the incident is under way. Further details are awaited.Refuting the allegations, the media cell of the SP tweeted CCTV footage which it claimed showed that the child was hit by a "saffron-colored Roadways bus" after Akhilesh's convoy had already moved on from the area."The accident in Gorakhpur that the media, the BJP and the lying chief minister Adityanath are claiming was caused by a collision with a JCB, killing a child, was actually caused by a saffron-colored Roadways bus directly under the chief minister’s control. The CCTV footage clearly shows the Roadways bus hitting that child on the road," the SP said in a post on X."Since the child’s father is a BJP member, chief minister Adityanath and the BJP together got him to make a false statement and gave him and the child’s family a false account of what happened, which misled the family into starting to blame the Samajwadi Party. But the CCTV footage reveals the whole truth. Uncontrolled, dilapidated Roadways buses keep running over innocent people every day, but the chief minister, who collects the full fare, doesn’t bat an eyelid. All he has done to fulfill his responsibility is have the buses painted saffron. I don’t know how he has the nerve to stand on stage and lie. The truth is out, and the shamelessness of the chief minister and all the BJP members has been exposed. The media channels that were running false news at the BJP’s behest have also been exposed," it added.
Article Summary: A Aryavardhan Singh, 12, was killed after being run over by a bulldozer. The bulldozer was returning from a Samajwadi Party roadshow led by Akhilesh Yadav. The incident triggered a sharp reaction from the Uttar Pradesh BJP, which alleged negligence in the conduct of the roadshow.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), one of the most anticipated video games in recent years, to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation, drawing a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6."India is playing a whole new game!" Modi said in a post on X, sharing a series of colourful graphics styled around the popular Grand Theft Auto video game franchise.Titled 'Between GTA V and VI, here's how India upgraded', the graphics compare India's position in several sectors during the period between the release of GTA V in 2013 and GTA VI in 2026. The comparison covers economic growth, poverty reduction, sanitation, renewable energy and the space sector.The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development over the past 13 years.One of the graphics compares India's economic position, describing the country as part of the 'Fragile Five' economies during the GTA V era and portraying it as the world's fastest-growing major economy in the GTA VI era.The comparison reflects India's changing economic position over the past decade, with the country emerging as a major growth centre in the global economy.Another graphic focuses on poverty reduction, showing extreme poverty declining from 27% in the 'Then' category to 2.6% in the 'Now' category.The illustration contrasts a cluster of thatched houses with a modern home and a family, presenting the change as an indicator of improvements in living conditions.The graphics also highlight India's sanitation drive, showing sanitation mission completion rising from 39% to 100%.The comparison features children using dustbins and a public sanitation facility, alongside the Swachh Bharat Mission logo.The renewable energy sector is another focus of the post. The graphic shows India's solar capacity increasing from 2.82 GW to 175 GW.It contrasts workers installing solar panels with a large solar power installation, presenting the expansion of renewable energy infrastructure as another marker of India's transformation.The final comparison focuses on India's space sector and the growth of private participation in space technology.The graphic shows the number of space startups increasing from one during the earlier period to 440 in the present, depicting workers assembling a rocket in a modern manufacturing facility.The comparison reflects the expansion of India's private space ecosystem following the opening up of the sector to private players.Meanwhile, Congress on took a swipe at PM Modi after he invoked the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, or GTA 6, saying it was very appropriate as the video game follows a “criminal duo”.Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said, “The PM, in a desperate bid to reach out to the youth, has resorted to GTA V and GTA VI imagery on social media.”“Recall that this video game follows a criminal duo. How very appropriate,” he said on X.An action-adventure game developed and published by Rockstar Games, Grand Theft Auto VI was rolled out across the globe on Thursday, marking its entry into the GTA series following 2013's Grand Theft Auto V.PM Modi's post coincides with the global release of Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026, ending a 13-year wait since Grand Theft Auto V was released in September 2013.Developed by Rockstar Games, GTA VI returns players to Vice City, a fictionalised version of Miami, and follows the story of protagonists Jason and Lucia. The game is launching on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.The long gap between the two instalments has made GTA VI one of the most anticipated entertainment releases, with Rockstar building expectations through trailers, promotional campaigns and pre-release announcements.By using the franchise's return as a timeline, Modi's post draws a parallel between the evolution of the gaming series and India's development across economic, infrastructure and technology sectors over the same period.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi used the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) to showcase India's economic and infrastructure transformation. He drew a comparison between the country's progress during the 13-year gap between GTA V and GTA 6. The post uses the gaming franchise's long-awaited return as a reference point to present India's development.

Odisha has stepped up preparations as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast, with nearly 3 lakh people evacuated, hundreds of rescue personnel deployed and thousands of shelters readied.The IMD has forecast that the storm is likely to make landfall between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon, with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph.2,98,676 people had been evacuated to safer locations across Odisha by Thursday evening, PTI reported, quoting Sspecial relief commissioner(SRC) Rajesh P Patil. The state has set up 2,523 relief camps and prepared 9,341 cyclone shelters.A total of 423 rescue teams have been deployed in vulnerable areas. These include 60 Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) teams, 14 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 131 Fire and Emergency Services teams. The Coast Guard has also been asked to keep helicopters, vessels and other logistical support ready.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast that Cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the Odisha coast between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon or afternoon.IMD director general Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said the system was expected to cross as a cyclonic storm, with wind speeds of 90-100 kmph. Winds of 70-80 kmph are likely along parts of the Odisha coast, with the system expected to weaken as it moves northwards.The cyclone was around 410 km from Gopalpur and 470 km from Puri on Thursday evening, moving at a speed of 13 kmph, according to an IMD official.Odisha chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi chaired an emergency midnight review meeting at the Special Relief Commissioner's (SRC) office in Bhubaneswar to take stock of the state's final preparations for Cyclone Akvan."Today, I reviewed the preparations for the cyclone. According to information received from the IMD, the cyclone is now expected to make landfall along the Odisha coast... The situation has now become clearer. Based on this, we have intensified our preparations across 20 districts," Majhi said.He said evacuation to safer locations was progressing rapidly following earlier reviews and discussions with district magistrates of the 20 districts.Of the 9,341 cyclone shelters prepared across the state, 2,623 are currently operational, the chief minister said.The state has also identified 941 landslide-prone locations across six districts, primarily in hilly areas. "All teams are fully prepared to handle any eventuality," Majhi said.These include Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput and Malkangiri, with Gajapati accounting for 211 locations.Rail services have been disrupted as a precaution. East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29, while the South Eastern Railway cancelled 28 express trains, mostly those operating to and from Puri.Tourists have been barred from visiting Gopalpur, Puri, Satapada and Chilika. Schools have also been closed in districts under red, orange and yellow weather alerts.The Gundicha Temple in Puri will remain closed from November 19 to 21, while the Jagannath Temple will remain open. Nandankanan Zoological Park and Botanical Garden have been closed on November 19 and 20. Bhitarkanika National Park will remain shut until November 21, and Similipal National Park on November 20 and 21.Neighbouring Andhra Pradesh has also stepped up preparedness. The IMD has issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, an orange alert for Parvathipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli, and a yellow alert for Kakinada.At Paradip Port, six fishing boats carrying 54 fishermen have been provided safe harbour, ANI reported. In Balasore, the district administration has identified 145 permanent cyclone shelters and 1,250 temporary shelters. District magistrate Suryawanshi Mayur Vikas said teams were ready to relocate 12,000-15,000 people, with a contingency plan to evacuate up to 2.5 lakh if required.The IMD has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in parts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh, with heavy to very heavy rainfall likely in Visakhapatnam and adjoining districts. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea until the morning of November 21.Nearly a month after the monsoon withdrew in mid-October, Tripura is bracing for scattered rain and isolated thunderstorms as Cyclone Akvan's outer cloud bands draw moisture into the Northeast.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast isolated thunderstorms and gusty winds of 30-40 kmph across the state on Thursday and Friday, with some areas likely to see thunderstorm activity on November 22. A yellow alert has been issued for South Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala for Thursday.Isolated heavy rainfall is also expected in West Tripura, Sepahijala, Gomati and South Tripura on Friday and Saturday. The IMD has ruled out any threat of a direct cyclone strike or severe winds in the state.Akvan is moving towards the Odisha and north Andhra Pradesh coasts and remains far from Tripura. Its indirect influence is expected to keep weather conditions unsettled for the next few days. Temperatures are likely to remain near normal, with foggy conditions possibly setting in next week and a sharper winter chill expected in early December.Read More: Cyclone Akvan Live Updates
Article Summary: Odisha has stepped up preparations as Cyclone Akvan approaches the coast. Nearly 3 lakh people evacuated, hundreds of rescue personnel deployed and thousands of shelters readied. Storm is likely to make landfall between Puri and Gopalpur around Friday noon.

AMRITSAR: As Sonia Gandhi ’s memoir,, brings renewed attention to her personal journey and family history, a Sikh man has an unusual connection to her past.Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum dedicated to her family and early life.Located in Lusiana, a village in Italy’s Vicenza province in the Veneto region, the house has gradually emerged as a point of interest for visitors, particularly from India. Kang has put up a board outside the property identifying it as the “Indian House, Place of Birth, 9 December 1946, Sonia Gandhi”.Kang, who lives with his wife, son and daughter in Brescia, about an hour’s drive from Lusiana, said he purchased the property in 2020 but declined to disclose its price. He said the family had decided to convert it into a museum and had now obtained the necessary permissions to take the project forward. With Sonia Gandhi’s memoir drawing public attention to her personal journey, he feels this is the right time to develop the property as a museum.“We want to meet Sonia Gandhi and her children, Rahul and Priyanka, to learn more about the family’s story and understand which personal belongings and other articles could be displayed in the museum. We want visitors to get a glimpse of her family background and early life,” Kang told TOI during his visit to Amritsar on Thursday.Born into an ordinary family in Lusiana, Sonia Gandhi’s journey has been extraordinary. Kang said her father, Stefano Maino, was a mason and building contractor, and there was little in her early life to suggest that she would one day emerge as one of the most influential women in Indian politics.From a modest Italian village, she went on to marry Rajiv Gandhi, become the wife of a Prime Minister, and eventually lead the Indian National Congress, one of the world's largest political parties. Her association with the Nehru-Gandhi family placed her at the centre of one of India's most influential political dynasties, marking a remarkable journey from a small-town upbringing to the corridors of power.Kang said the family would be delighted if Sonia Gandhi and her children visited the property. “We are proud owners of Sonia Gandhi’s house. It is their family home, and we are ready to hand over the keys whenever they wish to come,” he said, adding that people known to the family in the village were also eager to meet her.Stating that over the years, the property has become a talking point among villagers, Kang said locals immediately identify it as “Sonia Gandhi’s house” whenever they see visitors from India, particularly Sikhs, understanding that they have come to see the former Congress president’s ancestral home.The growing tourist interest has also benefited the village economy, with visitors spending money at local eateries and accommodation facilities. Several prominent residents, including politicians, had attended the house’s inauguration, he said. The family also organises a function every year on Sonia Gandhi’s birthday, he added.Kang said he spends 100 euros a month on a caretaker and pays around 1,000 euros annually in property taxes. Despite suggestions from some people to rent out the house for more than 800 euros a month or convert it into a gurdwara, the family has refused.“We do not want to rent out our prized possession or change its character. We intend to preserve it as a place associated with Sonia Gandhi’s family,” he said.Asked about Sikh hardliners who hold the Gandhi family responsible for Operation Bluestar, Kang dismissed their criticism, saying only a handful of such elements were pursuing their own separatist agenda. He maintained that the operation was a decision of the government of the day and that blaming the Gandhi family personally for it was misplaced.For Kang, the property is not merely a real estate acquisition but an opportunity to preserve a small piece of the personal history of one of India's most prominent political figures.
Article Summary: Sukhdev Singh Kang claims to have purchased the Maino family's ancestral home in Italy, which he says is Sonia Gandhi’s birthplace. Born on December 9, 1946, the former Congress president spent her early years in the Italian village, and Kang is now preparing to convert the six-room property into a museum.

No. The attitude remains: 'Modiji, you do it, we will see'," PM said at the Ficci AGM. He said tax relief to individuals had helped boost consumption and govt had reduced GST rates and speeded up I-T refunds, freeing up money that was earlier stuck for months. The comments came amid fresh demands for tax sops in the upcoming budget with business leaders submitting their wish list to the FM.Businesses are citing cost pressure and weakening demand amid signs of a pick-up in investment.While PM Narendra Modi cited India's rapid growth, he also called upon industry captains to suggest more reform proposals. "I have come because I respect you. But your experience with previous govts has been so bitter that I am paying the price for it. This is not that old govt. This is a friendly govt... Without hesitation and without inhibition, write to me openly and tell me what reforms are still needed."While urging industry to think beyond the domestic market and produce quality products, he asked them "seize the opportunity" offered by the trade agreements that are being signed.At the same time, he reiterated his message to promote 'swadeshi', citing the call made by Mahatma Gandhi in 1930, and flagged pharma, steel and aluminium among sectors for a domestic manufacturing push."Everyone is sitting here and knows this. India is known as the 'pharmacy of the world'. Yet, despite this, India imports APIs, bulk drugs, and drug intermediates worth billions of dollars every year. There are hundreds of such categories where we still depend on imports. Our pharmaceutical industry must understand which ingredients can be produced within India... We already have strength in finished medicines.Now we must also build capability in ingredients." He also called upon industry to step up investment in agriculture.Besides, he suggested that companies look beyond their comfort zone and enter areas that are strategic."Industry must also prepare for the demands that will emerge in the future at both the national and global levels. We must work on those capabilities that, in this era of weaponisation of resources, become all of our responsibility to secure the nation's future. Therefore, my request to you is this: in every long-term investment decision over the next 20 years, make 'India First' your foundation. This will make the country self-reliant and will also open new opportunities for the growth of your businesses. "
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi admonished the corporate sector for not passing on the benefit of reduced corporate tax to employees. NEW DELHI: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle-age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests.Under the new rules, notified on November 13, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity, while older vehicles will have to undergo emission tests at shorter intervals. The revised framework also standardises PUC certificate validity for older emission categories across the country, replacing variations in testing requirements between states.The changes have been introduced through the Central Motor Vehicles (Sixteenth Amendment) Rules, 2026, which amend Rule 115(7) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The amendment came into force on the date of its publication in the Official Gazette.Previously, the validity of a PUC certificate was determined primarily by the vehicle's Bharat Stage (BS) emission category. Consequently, a newly registered private car and an older commercial vehicle, despite belonging to the BS-VI category, were both eligible for a certificate valid for one year.The revised framework introduces a more differentiated approach for BS-VI vehicles. Certificate validity will now depend on two factors:The vehicle's age will be calculated from the date of its first registration.Under the earlier system, all private BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for 12 months, irrespective of their age.The revised rules introduce three validity brackets:This means owners of newer private BS-VI vehicles will have to undergo emission testing less frequently, while those with vehicles older than 10 years will face more frequent testing.Commercial BS-VI vehicles will also be subject to an age-based validity schedule, although the extension for newer vehicles will be shorter than that available to private vehicles.Previously, all commercial BS-VI vehicles received PUC certificates valid for one year. Under the amended rules:The revised schedule therefore offers longer validity to newer commercial vehicles, but retains more frequent testing requirements for older ones.The amendment also introduces a uniform testing requirement for vehicles conforming to older emission standards.Previously, BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles were generally subject to a six-month PUC certificate validity under the central rules. However, some states had prescribed shorter intervals. Delhi, for instance, already required these vehicles to undergo emission testing every three months.Under the revised framework, the validity period for all BS-I, BS-II and BS-III vehicles will be three months, irrespective of their age or category.This makes the three-month testing requirement applicable uniformly across all states and Union territories.For BS-IV vehicles, the earlier central provision allowed a PUC certificate validity of 12 months. However, certain states and areas within the national capital region (NCR) had already imposed a shorter six-month validity.The amended rules now prescribe six months as the standard validity period for all BS-IV vehicles across the country, irrespective of whether they are private or commercial.The change effectively brings the national requirement in line with the stricter timelines already followed in some regions.The amendment also clarifies how the validity period of a renewed PUC certificate will be calculated, depending on when the vehicle owner undergoes the emission test.Renewal within 10 days before expiry: If the vehicle undergoes testing within the 10 days preceding the expiry of its existing certificate, the renewed certificate will take effect from the expiry date of the previous certificate. This ensures that owners do not lose any remaining validity by renewing early.Renewal on or after expiry: If the test is conducted on or after the existing certificate's expiry date, the renewed certificate will be valid from the date of the test.PUC certificates issued before the amended rules came into force will remain valid until their respective expiry dates.Vehicle owners do not need to obtain fresh certificates immediately to comply with the revised schedule. The new validity provisions will apply when they renew their existing certificates for the first time under the amended rules.For instance, a private BS-VI car that is four years old and currently holds a one-year PUC certificate will become eligible for a three-year certificate at its next renewal. The revised validity will not automatically extend the certificate it already holds.All vehicles must have a valid PUC certificate issued by a testing centre authorised by the respective state government.Under Rule 116 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, vehicle owners are required to produce the certificate when demanded by an authorised official. Its validity can also be verified digitally through the Parivahan PUCC Portal.Under the earlier provisions, new vehicles across emission categories were exempt from obtaining a separate PUC certificate for the first year following their initial registration. However, the available details of the latest amendment do not clarify whether this exemption has been altered or retained.
Article Summary: The ministry of road transport and highways (MoRTH) has revised the validity period of pollution under control (PUC) certificates. It introduced a vehicle- age-based system that will determine how frequently vehicles must undergo emission tests. Under the new rules, newer BS-VI vehicles will be eligible for longer certificate validity. Older vehicles will have to undergo tests at shorter intervals.

Article Title: SC: Assess buyer's liability before home loan recovery
Article Text:
NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the “unholy” bank-builder nexus, said SC

NEW DELHI: In a big relief to lakhs of homebuyers, SC has ruled that in housing projects that remained incomplete despite banks releasing major portion of loan instalments to rogue or insolvent builders, the commercial courts, NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the "unholy" bank-builder nexus.The order came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on a petition by homebuyers in Krishna housing project, Gurgaon, by Raheja Developers, which has gone into insolvency proceedings.The petitioners said the bank had started recovery proceedings against them in a commercial court in Saket, New Delhi, even though they had not yet got their flats.The CJI-led bench said, "It is the bounden duty of the commercial court to determine the nexus between the builder and bank officials and to see whether the bank disbursed the loan amount to the builder strictly in terms of the tripartite agreement."It said unless a categorical finding is returned that the homebuyers are in default, no interim direction regarding payment of instalments can be issued. "We direct the civil court not to take any coercive action against the petitioners or similarly placed homebuyers without first determining the above-mentioned issue," it said.As per the tripartite agreement between buyers-builder-banks, the financier was to disburse the loan amount directly to the builder in proportion to the progress in construction on ground.However, in many cases, because of builder-bank officials nexus, the financial institutions released loan amounts against each flat buyer much more than the money that should have been disbursed to the builder given the stage of construction of the housing project.When the project remained incomplete for decades, the bank filed recovery suits against homebuyers who, without getting the flats, kept paying EMIs and house rent. A decree in the suit would mean fastening crippling financial liability on the homebuyers.In Sept last year, a Justice Kant-led bench ordered a CBI inquiry against a large number of builders and banks across India for colluding to misuse the tripartite subvention scheme and fleece the homebuyers even when the projects remained incomplete for decades.On Thursday, the bench found its sympathy for the homebuyers has virtually opened the floodgates of litigation and thousands of them suffering under the tyranny of builders and banks have rushed directly to SC. It said, "Our hands are full and we may not be able to handle fresh litigation."In a similar case from Bengaluru involving over 4,000 homebuyers, it protected homebuyers against possible recovery proceedings from banks as the housing project remained incomplete for nearly a decade despite the petitioners paying 95% of the cost of the flat. After granting protection, the bench asked the petitioner's counsel to move Karnataka HC for appropriate relief.
Article Summary: Commercial courts, NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the "unholy" bank-builder nexus. The order came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on a petition by homebuyers in Gurgaon.

Article Title: Next door, worlds apart: India's child malnutrition puzzle
Article Text:
AI generated picture

Good news nationally, with a catch

India's fight against child malnutrition is showing progress, but not on every front. While fewer children are falling behind in height, weight-related problems remain stubbornly persistent.

Does living near a big city help?

India's latest child nutrition data reveals striking inequalities even between neighbouring districts

The districts that were carved out

What lies behind the gap

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A common refrain in India is that birth is a lottery, where a child is born can, in many ways, determine how their childhood is shaped, if not their entire life. But even children born in neighbouring districts may have very different courses in life. This interesting facet has emerged from an analysis of district-wise malnutrition data published in the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-6).In Nagpur district, roughly one in five children under five is classified as stunted, or too short for their age under standard child-growth measures. In neighbouring Chandrapur, also in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, it is more than two in five. The latest survey puts childhood stunting at 20.2% in Nagpur and 42.4% in Chandrapur. The two neighbouring districts show remarkably divergent statistics.The previous survey makes the gap harder to explain. In NFHS-5, conducted in 2019–21, Nagpur's figure was 27.6% and Chandrapur's 37.3%. Since then, Nagpur's estimate has fallen and Chandrapur's has risen.In November 2025, TOI reported on a programme for 915 mothers and children through 27 Anganwadi centres in Chandrapur's Jiwati taluka. The people running it described low literacy, reliance on subsistence farming and little variety in children's food.It is a reflection on how authorities are trying to reverse the worrying trend.The World Health Organization links stunting to poorer learning and school performance, more frequent illness and lower wages in adulthood. The first 1,000 days, from conception to a child's second birthday, are particularly critical. Growth lost during this period can have lasting consequences. While some catch-up growth is possible, full recovery is often difficult.India has made a substantial gain against stunting, which reflects the effects of poor nutrition, repeated illness and other disadvantages over a child's early years. The national estimate fell from 35.5% in NFHS-5 to 29.3% in NFHS-6.Children's weight-related indicators have barely changed, though. Wasting — being too thin for one's height — went from 19.3% to 19%. Underweight prevalence, which reflects both long-term and more recent nutritional problems, remained nearly flat, going from 32.1% to 31.8%. Severe wasting did fall, from 7.7% to 5.2%. Put simply, fewer of India's children are now classified as too short for their age, but almost one in five is still too thin for their height.TOI compared published figures for 680 districts and single-district Union territories with usable estimates for all three principal measures in both rounds. In 235, all three percentages were lower in the newer survey. In 196, stunting was lower but wasting and underweight were both higher.Vidarbha is not an exception. In Madhya Pradesh's Malwa belt, Indore reports 22.8% stunting, against 38.6% in neighbouring Dhar. The share of underweight children is 30.8% in Indore and 53.2% in Dhar, where more than half of young children are underweight.In Maharashtra's Marathwada, Beed's stunting estimate is 24.8%, while Hingoli's is 43.1%. In Odisha's KBK region, the historically disadvantaged belt associated with Kalahandi, Balangir and Koraput, Kalahandi reports 26.9% and Rayagada 47.2%. The two districts share a boundary.Often, it appears to. Nationally, stunting is estimated at 23.9% among urban children, compared with 30.9% among rural children. Look at Nagpur or Indore, and the obvious explanation might be jobs, hospitals and markets. Lucknow, too, reports a lower figure than neighbouring Sitapur: 31% against 45.5%.Tamil Nadu, though, bucks the trend. Coimbatore has a major industrial city, yet its district stunting estimate is 28%, compared with 15.6% in neighbouring Tiruppur, itself an industrial centre. The same is true in Bihar. Patna district, which contains the state capital, records 42.7% stunting, more than neighbouring Vaishali's 36.1%. On the underweight measure, the pattern reverses: Patna's estimate is 29.8% against Vaishali's 36.4%. A district with a large city also includes the villages beyond it, and its average mixes both.Research backs up the complexity of this relationship. A study of more than 443,000 children using earlier NFHS rounds found strong associations between stunting and household resources and mothers' education. After accounting for other characteristics, urban residence on its own was not a consistent predictor in the later rounds. A family's circumstances counted for more than its address.The clearest example is in Gujarat, where an official report acknowledged that averages were hiding disadvantage.Until September 2007, Tapi was part of Surat. The old district combined Surat's large urban economy with remote tribal areas. A Gujarat government human-development report, published in 2015, said combining them in one statistical profile had obscured conditions in places needing more development attention. Tapi was created from five predominantly tribal rural talukas. At the 2011 Census, Scheduled Tribes made up about 84% of its population.In NFHS-6, the stunting difference is relatively small: 30.4% in Surat and 33.9% in Tapi. The gap shows up in weight. Wasting stands at 14.1% in Surat versus 26.9% in Tapi, where more than one child in four is too thin for their height. Underweight prevalence is 32.2% versus 43.9%.The same pattern appears where other districts were divided. Chhota Udaipur, carved out of Vadodara in 2013, reports 51.5% stunting, affecting more than half its young children, compared with Vadodara's 35.5%. Palghar, separated from Thane in 2014, reports 42%, against Thane's 29%. State government figures based on the 2011 Census put the Scheduled Tribe share at 37.39% in Palghar and 5.27% in the reorganised Thane district. Palghar itself spans the urbanising Vasai–Virar belt and remote settlements, so its average hides further differences within the district.In Haryana, Nuh was formed in 2005 from five blocks of the former Gurgaon district. The region had been receiving special development attention well before that: Haryana established the Mewat Development Board in 1980. Today, the stunting estimates for Nuh and neighbouring Gurugram are 46% and 21.6%. The survey's separate measure of adequate diets among children aged six to 23 months also shows a wide gap, at 8.1% and 19.6%.Mizoram has a similar case. Mamit was carved out of Aizawl district in 1998. The latest stunting figures are 41.2% in Mamit and 23.1% in Aizawl. The Mamit administration's 2011 Census profile identifies it as one of the state's least urbanised districts.NFHS-6 found that just 15.3% of children aged six to 23 months nationally met its standard for an adequate diet, based on a combination of food groups and feeding frequency. That is up from 11% in the previous survey. It still means more than eight in ten children at that age miss out on enough variety in their food, enough meals in a day, or both.Family circumstances show up clearly in the data. An analysis of NFHS-5 found stunting among about 46% of children whose mothers had no formal education, compared with 23% among children whose mothers had higher education — half the rate. Education overlaps with household wealth, maternal health and living conditions, so this is an association, and the separate effects are hard to untangle.There are limits to these comparisons. NFHS is not a census of every child, and its rounds do not follow the same children. District estimates have sampling uncertainty, which this analysis has not independently quantified. Research using earlier surveys has also found that the season of measurement affects wasting. Yet, as India looks to become more prosperous, the onus is on ensuring that none of the next generation falls through the cracks. That would be a big step towards becoming a developed nation.
Article Summary: India's fight against child malnutrition is showing progress, but not on every front. While fewer children are falling behind in height, weight-related problems remain stubbornly persistent. India has made a substantial gain against stunting, which reflects the effects of poor nutrition, repeated illness and other disadvantages over a child's early years.

Article Title: UNFPA puts India's population at 1.47 billion in 2026, calls for investment in 'youth dividend'
