NEW DELHI: Continuing to be the most populous country in the world, India’s population for 2026 is estimated to be 1.47 billion (147.66) crores with the population doubling time of 81 years, according to the UNFPA’s State of The World Population Report 2026 released on Thursday. India’s population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now.India’s population was 1.46 billion in 2025, 1.44 billion in the year before that. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be India’s “youth moment” and calling for investing while the dividend window is open.Surpassing China, India became the world’s most populous country with 142.86 crore people in 2023 with China falling behind India with a population of 142.57 crore.Meanwhile, China’s estimated mid - year population for 2026 stands at 1.41 billion (141.29 crores) with 70% of the population in the 15-64 years bracket. 15% of China’s population is 65 and above. Fertility rate stands at 1.0 and life expectancy is high at 76 for men and 82 for women.The demographic indicators show that in India those in the 0-14 years age group account for 24% of the population; for 10-19 years this is 17% and for 10-24 it is a strong 26% reflecting India’s youth dividend.The data shows that 69% of India’s population is in the 15-64 years bracket and the population aged 65 and older account for 8%.Life expectancy for males is 71 years and that for females is 74. If one looks at world population in 2026 it is estimated at 8.3 billion with population doubling time 84 years. Globally life expectancy at birth stands at 71 for men and 76 for women.The report, flags India’s Total Fertility Rate at 1.9, the same as last year, which is below the replacement level fertility of 2.1 births per woman indicating that women are having fewer children than needed to maintain the population size from one generation to the next.The 2026 report also draws on UNFPA’s global Demographic Futures Survey of more than 108,000 internet-connected adults in 73 countries, including 1,722 in India to highlight aspirations around relationships, parenthood and life goals, and the conditions that influence people’s ability to realise them.It further states that young people’s aspirations regarding family and relationships will play a central role in shaping the nation’s demographic trajectory.Survey findings from India show that optimism runs high with 83% of respondents feeling positive or very positive about the future, despite concerns about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality, UNFPA highlights. Women aged 18 to 39 describe an ideal family size of 2.1 children and parenthood remains a strong aspiration: nearly 85% of childless respondents aged 35 to 39 would ideally like to become parents.“Young people need confidential, non-judgmental ‘Sexual Reproductive Health’ information and services (contraception, menstrual health, STI prevention, referral) alongside pre-pregnancy, maternal and postnatal care,” UNFPA states while emphasising the need for India to expand and strengthen youth-responsive primary care.
Article Summary: India’s population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be India's ‘youth moment’

SRINAGAR: Three leopards, including two female cubs aged 8-9 months, were found dead in the forests of north Kashmir’s Kunzar area, prompting J&K’s wildlife protection department to file an FIR Thursday against unknown people after autopsies raised suspicion of poisoning.Wildlife official Shahid Sultan said the cubs were found dead on Nov 17, with no visible injury marks. NEW DELHI: Malaysia could, from Jan 1, 2027, withdraw its visa exemption policy for Indian visitors. The southeast Asian country had in Dec 2023 started this to boost tourism post Covid. While the immigration department of Malaysia announced last month “Indian nationals entering Malaysia from (Jan 1, 2027) onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival,” the Malaysian High Commission in Delhi told TOI Thursday the “visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026.” Which means unless that facility is extended, going to Malaysia will require a visa from next year.While there was a surge in Indians visiting the country, the High Commission of India (HCI) in Kuala Lumpur had recently warned that there had been “a noticeable increase in Indian nationals arriving in Malaysia using the 30-day visa-free facility, to seek employment.” This, HCI had warned, “is a clear violation of immigration rules, as the visa-free entry facility which permits Indian passport holders to stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days is granted for tourism and social visits only.The immigration department of Malaysia (JIM) said in an announcement dated Nov 17, 2026: “…visa exemption facility for Indian nationals will no longer be available with effect from Jan 1, 2027. Accordingly, Indian nationals entering Malaysia from this date onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa prior to their arrival. Visa applications may be submitted through the MyVISA portal starting Dec 1, 2026.” Other countries whose citizens require visa to enter Malaysia include Bangladesh, Bhutan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and Nepal.The Malaysian High Commission in New Delhi told TOI Thursday: “Currently all Indian passport holders are allowed to enter and stay in Malaysia for up to 30 days only (for each entry) without any visa for tourism, business or social visits purposes. This Malaysia visa-free (visa exemption facility) period tentatively ends on Dec 31, 2026. Therefore, Indian Nationals entering Malaysia from Jan 1, 2027, onwards will be required to obtain a valid visa before arrival. ”Going visa free for Indians in Dec 2023 had led to Malaysia seeing a spike in visitor numbers from here. From just over 7.3 lakh Indian tourists in pre-Covid 2019, the number rose to 13.6 lakh in 2024; 15.6 lakh in 2025 and 7.4 lakh in Jan-June 2026 with a target of 21 lakh for this full calendar year.However, HCI, Kuala Lumpur had in a X post on Sept 22, 2026, warned against the misuse of tourist visas. “…Many Indian nationals are misled by unscrupulous agents with false job promises, leading to overstay, illegal status, exploitation, detention and legal action. Genuine tourists must carry valid and verifiable documentation such as confirmed return ticket, hotel booking, online submission of the Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC) three days before the arrival date, and a passport with minimum 6-month validity, to avoid any immigration-related issues on arrival in Malaysia.Once again, Indian nationals are strictly advised not to travel to Malaysia for work / employment purpose without work permit or visa with reference (VDR),” the HCI post had added.The Malaysian immigration dept announcement of Nov 17 adds: “…all visa processing fees paid are strictly non-refundable, regardless of the application outcome, change of policy or any subsequent change to travel plans. JIM reserves the right to amend these entry requirements at any time in accordance with directives from govt of Malaysia.”

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has permitted the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, Tamil Nadu, on November 24, 2026, as an interim arrangement.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi, however, stayed portions of the Madras high court judgment that had upheld the direction to restore the practice of lighting the lamp at the Deepathoon. The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah over ownership of the hilltop and the location of the ritual.The development follows arguments by the dargah before the top court on Thursday, when it claimed ownership of the entire hilltop and opposed the demand to light the lamp at the stone pillar. The hearing on the matter had remained inconclusive, with the court scheduled to continue proceedings on Friday.Senior advocate Amit Anand Tiwari, appearing for the dargah, referred to a 1920 judicial order passed in a civil suit and said there were findings establishing that the flight of stairs from Nellithope to the hill belonged to the shrine."The entire top of the hill belongs to the dargah. There is no question of lighting the deepam at the top of the hill, where the stone pillar is situated, irrespective of what the distance between the dargah and the stone pillar is," Tiwari said.He also submitted that the "whole of the top of the hillock on which the mosque and the flagstaff stand" as well as the stone pillar are located is the property of the dargah.The controversy centres on the location of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lighting ceremony at the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple in Thiruparankundram. For decades, the festival lamp has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple on the lower slopes of the hill.Hindu groups have sought permission to light the lamp at the Deepathoon, an ancient stone pillar higher up the hill and around 50 metres from the dargah. The dispute has led to legal proceedings over the location of the ritual and ownership of the hill.The Tamil Nadu government had opposed the demand, arguing that permitting the lighting of the lamp near the dargah could create wider legal and administrative complications. On Wednesday, it told the Supreme Court that allowing the practice could lead to thousands of survey pillars across the country acquiring a religious character.The dargah committee had also challenged the procedure followed by the Madras High Court. Senior advocate Huzefa Ahmadi, appearing for the committee, argued that a single-judge bench had passed its order without giving the dargah adequate time to file a reply under the high court rules. He also submitted that the judge had conducted a site visit without notifying the dargah before passing the order.The Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) department has opposed a petition seeking to bring the temple and the entire Thiruparankundram hill under the control of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI).In an affidavit before the Supreme Court, HR&CE Commissioner T G Vinay said the temple's ownership and existing religious practices had been settled through decades of judicial proceedings. He maintained that the hill was owned by the Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple to the extent recognised by a civil court decree of 1923, which was subsequently restored by the Privy Council in 1931.The affidavit opposed three reliefs sought by petitioner Hindu Dharma Parishad: handing over the entire temple and hill to the ASI, keeping a lamp burning round the clock at the stone pillar described as the Deepathoon, and illuminating the entire hill with lamps during Karthigai Deepam."A title so settled cannot be disturbed and the administration of a religious endowment entrusted by statute to the HR&CE cannot be wrested away and handed over to the ASI upon a petition that pleads no ground in law and seeks the relief in the teeth of a concluded civil adjudication of title," the affidavit had said.On the lighting ceremony, the HR&CE commissioner maintained that the festival lamp had traditionally been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchipillaiyar temple, and not at the hilltop or the stone pillar.The department also referred to historical records of attempts made in 1862 and 1912 to light lamps near the hill's summit, where the dargah is situated. It argued that archaeological protection at Thiruparankundram covered specified features, including the rock-cut cave and inscriptions, and did not extend to the entire hill or the functioning temple.The department cautioned that allowing lamps to be lit at multiple locations, particularly near the dargah, could disrupt existing arrangements and create law-and-order challenges at a site with a history of communal tension.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has permitted the lighting of the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp at the Deepathoon, a stone pillar on Thiruparankundram Hill in Madurai, Tamil Nadu. The interim permission comes amid a dispute between Hindu worshippers and the Hazrat Sultan Sikandar Badusha Auliya Dargah. The dispute has led to legal proceedings over the location of the ritual and ownership of the hill.

New Delhi: In a sweeping international crackdown, the Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) and the US Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) have dismantled the Indian nerve center of a massive transnational drug syndicate — shutting down an illicit pipeline flooding American streets with deadly opioids and psychotropic substances.​Under an operation code named, Monsoon Thunder, NCB teams carried out raids across multiple Indian cities —including Hyderabad, Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow — resulting in the arrest of six individuals linked to the network.The raids were carried on Nov 4 and Nov 13. Article Title: Centre moves to tighten controls on antibiotic manufacturing, bulk drug trade

In a move to tighten oversight of the pharmaceutical supply chain and tackle antimicrobial resistance (AMR), the Centre has proposed stricter controls on both the manufacturing and wholesale distribution of antibiotics and other bulk drugs. Under the proposed changes, fresh manufacturing licences for antimicrobials will require prior central approval, while wholesalers dealing in bulk drugs, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), will need a separate licence to improve monitoring of their movement.In a draft notification, the Union health ministry has proposed amending the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019, to include antimicrobials in the definition of a 'new drug'. This would require manufacturers seeking fresh licences to first obtain permission from the Central Licensing Authority (CLA) before approaching state licensing authorities for a manufacturing licence. Existing manufacturing licences will remain valid and will not require fresh central approval.The ministry's move follows concerns that antimicrobial manufacturing licences are being granted without adequate quality checks, including bioavailability, bioequivalence and stability studies.The proposed central scrutiny is aimed at ensuring the quality and efficacy of medicines, as substandard or ineffective antimicrobials can contribute to drug resistance and make infections harder to treat.Antimicrobial resistance occurs when bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites develop resistance to medicines used to treat infections, making treatment more difficult and increasing the risk of prolonged illness, complications and deaths.Separately, the ministry has proposed a separate application form and licence for bulk drug wholesalers under the Drugs Rules, 1945. Currently, a common wholesale licence covers both bulk drugs and finished medicines. The new framework will require sales to be supervised by a competent person and licences to specify the categories of bulk drugs handled, including those covered under the NDPS Act. The move aims to improve tracking, curb diversion of controlled substances and strengthen oversight of bulk antibiotics amid AMR concerns.The two proposals are part of the Centre's broader efforts to strengthen drug regulation and promote responsible antimicrobial use through a One Health approach, recognising the links between human, animal and environmental health.Both draft amendments are open to public and stakeholder comments before finalisation and are not yet in force. While the proposed manufacturing approval requirement will apply to fresh licences, existing bulk drug wholesale licence holders will get time to comply with the new requirements, which will take effect after expiry of their current retention period or 12 months from the final notification, whichever is later.
Article Summary: The Centre has proposed stricter controls on both the manufacturing and wholesale distribution of antibiotics and other bulk drugs. Fresh manufacturing licences for antimicrobials will require prior central approval. wholesalers dealing in bulk drugs, including active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), will need a separate licence.

Article Title: Nepal PM Balen Shah's first India visit on November 23, talks with PM Modi on agenda
Article Text:
Nepal PM Balen Shah

Indian ambassador meets Balendra Shah ahead of visit

Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will undertake a two-day State visit to India from November 22 to 23 at the invitation of Prime Minister Narendra Modi . The visit will include delegation-level talks, the inauguration of energy projects and discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation, Nepal's foreign secretary Amrit Bahadur Rai announced on Friday.A 34-member government delegation led by Shah will travel from Kathmandu to New Delhi for the high-level engagement, Rai said, according to news agency ANI. Shah is scheduled to hold delegation-level talks with PM Modi on Monday, November 23.Following the meeting, the two Prime Ministers will jointly inaugurate several energy-related projects. Bilateral agreements and other instruments covering different areas of cooperation will also be signed and exchanged, according to the announced itinerary.The two leaders are also scheduled to address a joint press conference, after which PM Modi will host a luncheon in honour of the visiting Nepali Prime Minister.During his stay in New Delhi, Shah will call on President Droupadi Murmu and pay tribute to Mahatma Gandhi at his memorial in Rajghat. He is also scheduled to attend the Nepal-India Business Forum, which is aimed at strengthening trade and economic ties between the neighbouring countries.A separate business delegation is also expected to travel to India alongside Shah and his official delegation.Shah received an invitation from PM Modi to visit India after his government, led by the Rastriya Swatantra Party, was formed in March. The government came to power around six months after youth-led Gen Z protests toppled the administration of former prime minister K P Sharma Oli in September last year.According to Nepal’s foreign affairs ministry sources quoted by news agency ANI, discussions during Shah’s visit are expected to cover rail, road and air connectivity, infrastructure development, cooperation, trade and tourism.The visit is also significant against the backdrop of the longstanding diplomatic convention under which newly elected Nepali prime ministers make India their first official bilateral foreign destination. However, the practice is not an absolute rule. Oli departed from the convention in 2024 when he chose China for his first official bilateral visit.Ahead of the visit, newly appointed Indian Ambassador to Nepal Sudhakar Dalela called on Shah on Wednesday and discussed preparations for the high-level engagement, the Indian Embassy in Nepal said in a statement shared on X.The embassy said Dalela conveyed PM Modi's greetings to the Nepali Prime Minister and briefed him on the preparations."Ambassador @SudhakarDalela called on Rt. Hon. Mr. Balendra Shah, Prime Minister of Nepal, today. Ambassador conveyed the greetings of Hon'ble PM Shri @narendramodi and shared details of ongoing preparations for the forthcoming high-level visit," the embassy said.It added that Shah thanked the Indian PM and the Indian government for the assistance extended to Nepal following the floods in the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi region."Rt. Hon. PM Balendra Shah conveyed his gratitude to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi and the Government of India for the support extended after the Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi flood," the embassy said.According to a readout from Nepal's Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, Shah also congratulated Dalela on his appointment and wished him a successful tenure. He enquired about the preparations for his India visit, while Dalela informed him that the agenda had been finalised.India and Nepal share close historical, cultural and geographical ties, supported by a 1,751-km open border and extensive people-to-people connections. The upcoming talks are expected to review bilateral cooperation, with energy, trade and economic engagement among the key areas on the agenda.
Article Summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah will undertake a two-day State visit to India from November 22 to 23. The visit will include delegation-level talks, the inauguration of energy projects and discussions on strengthening bilateral cooperation. A 34-member government delegation led by Shah will travel from Kathmandu to New Delhi for the high-level engagement.

Article Title: Supreme Court refuses separate listing of plea challenging split verdict on EC law
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined a request to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law governing the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners (ECs) should be heard by a larger bench.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the recall application, along with any challenge to the order referring the matter to a larger bench, could be considered by the five-judge Constitution bench already set up to hear the challenges to the law.The CJI also said the Constitution bench could hear the recall application even after one of the judges who delivered the split verdict retires.During the hearing, advocate Prashant Bhushan argued that the recall plea should be listed before the original bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma, which delivered the split verdict on September 23.Bhushan pointed out that Justice Sharma was due to retire next week. He also alleged that Justice Sharma had a conflict of interest and argued that the recall plea should be heard by the same bench.When the CJI suggested that the five-judge bench could examine the application, Bhushan said the order referring the matter to a larger bench had itself been challenged on the ground of an alleged conflict of interest.However, the CJI said Bhushan could raise these issues before the Constitution bench, which has been constituted to decide the validity of the 2023 law.The development follows a split verdict delivered on September 23 by Justices Datta and Sharma on whether the petitions challenging the law should be referred to a larger bench.At the centre of the challenge is the exclusion of the CJI from the panel responsible for selecting the CEC and Election Commissioners. Under the 2023 law, the selection panel comprises the Prime Minister, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union cabinet minister.While Justice Datta had held that the challenge could be heard by a two-judge bench, Justice Sharma favoured referring the matter to a five-judge Constitution bench, citing the important constitutional questions involved.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Friday declined a request to separately list a plea seeking recall of a split verdict on whether challenges to the 2023 law should be heard by a larger bench. A bench headed by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said the recall application could be considered by the five-judge Constitution bench already set up.

Article Title: 'Impossible for us to accept': Rahul Gandhi's response to question on Pakistan talks
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi at University of Chicago

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has ruled out bilateral talks with Pakistan until Islamabad stops supporting cross-border terrorism, saying India cannot engage in dialogue while its citizens continue to be killed in terror attacks.Speaking at the University of Chicago in Illinois on Wednesday, Gandhi was asked whether India and Pakistan could move beyond mutual accusations and explore cooperation. He said dialogue was possible, but Pakistan's alleged support for terrorism remained a major obstacle."There is scope, but there is a major problem, and that is Pakistan's support for and promotion of terrorism within our country. This is absolutely out of the question. It is impossible for us to accept a situation where our innocent people are being killed while we engage in talks with Pakistan. So, the moment that stops, then a conversation can potentially begin," he said.During the interaction, the Congress leader also spoke about India's economic challenges, arguing that the country was facing deep-rooted structural problems even before the recent Iran war.In a post on X, the Congress party highlighted three concerns raised during the discussion: concentration of wealth and power among a few large businesses, distress among small and medium-sized enterprises, and rising unemployment."India was already facing challenges like: Massive concentration of wealth and power in the hands of a few businesses, Large-scale destruction of small and medium-sized businesses, Unemployment. We could sense it and see it. The Iran war suddenly acted as a magnifying glass. So it pushed people over the edge," the post stated.Gandhi also cautioned against overlooking international developments and their impact on India, warning that the country could not remain insulated from global geopolitical shifts."We cannot remain unconcerned about what is happening in the rest of the world. If you think you are exempt from global geopolitics, you have a big problem coming," he said.Rahul Gandhi is on a two-day visit to the United States. He participated in a discussion at the University of Chicago with political science professor Robert Pape on Wednesday.A day earlier, he also took part in an academic interaction with students and faculty members at Columbia University in New York.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi says dialogue is possible, but Pakistan's alleged support for terrorism remains a major obstacle. Gandhi is on a two-day visit to the United States. He participated in a discussion at the University of Chicago with political science professor Robert Pape on Wednesday.

Article Title: Supreme Court declines Tamil Nadu's plea seeking 11 TMC Cauvery water from Karnataka
Article Text:
Supreme Court

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday declined to entertain Tamil Nadu 's petition seeking a direction to Karnataka to release 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of Cauvery water to make up for the alleged shortfall in its share.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Singh passed the order on the plea, in which Tamil Nadu sought additional water, citing the impact of water scarcity on farmers and crops in the state.Tamil Nadu had approached the top court seeking implementation of directions issued by the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA), which required Karnataka to release water to the neighbouring state.The state alleged that it had not been receiving its stipulated share of Cauvery water, resulting in a shortage that could affect agricultural activities and crops.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu sought a direction to Karnataka to release 11 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of Cauvery water. The state alleged that it had not been receiving its stipulated share of water. Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Singh passed the order on the plea.
